newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FUND SEES 5 RAND DLR, URGES S.AFRICA FX "BIG BANG".
newsitem.headline: FUND SEES 5 RAND DLR, URGES S.AFRICA FX "BIG BANG".

text.p: South Africa's rand is heading to 5.0 against the dollar and the country should adopt the "big bang" approach to scrapping foreign exchange controls, a leading international portfolio manager said on Thursday.

The rand, which is now stabilising again after another recent bout of weakness, is set to fall further, regardless of controls, said Hilary Wakefield, global portfolio manager at UK-based Old Mutual International Asset Managers.
"We are factoring five rand to the U.S. dollar in the short-term," he told a news briefing, adding that short-term meant the next three months.
The currency was trading around 4.70 on Thursday afternoon.
But despite current problems, Wakefield said foreign investment was waiting to enter the country -- and would be encouraged in by the lifting of controls.
"I think you will be surprised by the amount of foreign money waiting to come in," he said.
Asked if he favoured the immediate big bang approach over the government's previously-stated policy of being committed to an untimetabled phased withdrawal, he said: "Definitely".
The rand's collapse this year, which has seen it lose some 30 percent against the U.S. dollar since mid-February, and a sharp fall in reserves has fuelled wariness on lifting controls.
There are fears capital could flood from the country, forcing a further hike in already high interest rates.
The South African economy is already slowing down and higher rates could plunge it into a downturn.
But Wakefield said the risks were being exaggerated. "Interest rates will go up, but I don't think the situation will be as extreme as a lot of people are painting it," he said.
He added the current situation was also damaging as the government's willingess to support the rand with continued controls was attracting speculators to bet against the currency.
"It is a bit like a dam with a lot of leaks, but the leaks are just encouraging the speculators even more," he said.
Domestically, Old Mutual is South Africa's largest life assurer.
